acme-sre: Hey team — hitting a weird one with the embeddings endpoint. Our vector DB suddenly started rejecting inserts with a dimension mismatch. We expect 768-dims but the API returned 1024 for some calls.

acme-sre: This started after we turned on per-prefix caching to reduce cost. We're also batching requests in groups of 16. Latency has been fine but vectors are wrong.

Maya: Sorry you're seeing this — can you paste the exact request body you used and the response header+body? Also the model name and whether you used the `batch_size` param or client-side batching?

acme-sre: Pasting redacted payloads below. We call POST /v1/embeddings with 

```json
{"model":"open-embed-large-v2","input":["cust:order-123: the user visited ...","cust:order-124: other text ..."]}
```

acme-sre: Response (truncated):

```json
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.001,0.002,...],"index":0},{"embedding":[0.003,0.004,...],"index":1}],"model":"open-embed-large-v2"}
```

acme-sre: But the vector length is 1024 for index 0 and 768 for index 1. Vector DB checks length and fails for the first item. We didn't change the model.

Maya: Thanks. Two quick things: 1) Are you performing prefix reuse (you mentioned per-prefix caching) by passing a stable prefix string in the request or via app-level key? 2) Can you confirm tokenization/encoding of inputs is identical across requests?

acme-sre: We're using a short prefix label attached to each input: `cust:order-<id>:` — it's the same pattern for both items. We set header `X-Redwood-Cache: prefix=owner:project` to enable prefix caching.

Raj: jumping in from eng-ml — this looks like a cache key collision / prefix-reuse issue combined with batching. We recently rolled an optimization that allows cached prefix KV to be reused across requests to avoid recomputing sub-token contexts. The cache key should include model name + prefix hash + tokenization scheme + sequence length, but we found a path where sequence length wasn't included for small prefixes. That can cause the cached KV to be applied to a different quantized model variant (1024 vs 768 output dim) when a model alias is switched.

Raj: Can you repro with a single input (no batching) and with the header `X-Redwood-Cache: no-store`? That will tell us if caching is the culprit.

acme-sre: Tried that now. Single input with `no-store` returns 768 as expected. With `prefix=owner:project` cache enabled and batch=16 we reproduce the mixed dims ~20% of the time.

Lina: from eng-infra — adding logs from the serving runtime for one failing request: 

```
[2026-03-12T09:12:45Z] request_id=rid-9f2c model=open-embed-large-v2 batch_id=b-42 prefix_hash=ab12 cache_hit=true cached_kv_model=open-embed-large-v1 cached_kv_seq_len=40 runtime_model_variant=open-embed-large-v2 output_dim=1024
```

Lina: Notice cached_kv_model differs from runtime_model_variant — that's the key. Because the cache key omitted the exact model variant tag in an internal codepath, we allowed a KV computed for a previous model variant (open-embed-large-v1, 1024-dim) to be reused for a different runtime binary (v2, 768-dim). The runtime then mismatched shapes leading to the mixed-dimension vectors in a single batch.

Maya: Thanks Lina. Actionable steps for the customer while we patch: 1) Disable per-prefix caching (`X-Redwood-Cache: no-store`) 2) Avoid cross-request batching (use batch size = 1 or ensure all items share identical prefix+model variant) 3) Pin model to an exact variant name (no aliases) so model switches don't happen behind your back.

acme-sre: Those mitigations work for us. Quick Q: Is this a billing risk? We saw a bunch of retries and re-ingestion attempts into our DB.

Maya: Good question. Cache hits shouldn't charge for model compute, only the initial compute that populated the cache. But when cache reuse causes mismatched dimensions and you retry/append to DB, you may pay for multiple downstream write attempts. We'll audit your account for duplicate charges for the timeframe and credit if appropriate. I'll open a billing ticket.

Raj: Root cause summary for internal tracking: cache key generation omitted `model_variant_tag` for small prefixes in the `continuous-kv` path. When model aliasing/rollout happened, cached KV from an older variant (different embedding head size) was reused causing shape mismatch in batched responses (heterogeneous embeddings inside a single response). Also batching logic didn't validate homogeneous output dims per batch.

Raj: Short-term patch being deployed: include `model_variant_tag` and `seq_len` in the cache key, and add a fast validation that ensures all embeddings in a batch have identical length before returning — fall back to recompute per-item if mismatch detected. Expected rollout in the next 2 hours, hotfix backported to stable branch.

infra-bot: deploy started for `fix/embedding-cache-key` -> canary (10%) at 2026-03-12T09:45Z :rocket:
deploy-bot: canary passed health checks, progressive rollout to 50% at 2026-03-12T10:12Z

Maya: @acme-sre we've pushed the hotfix and added a transient check that rejects batches with mixed dims (returns 5xx with clear error) instead of returning mixed vectors. Can you verify in the next 20 minutes?

acme-sre: Verified — after the fix the earlier failing batch now returns a clean 768 for all items when cache enabled. Also confirmed DB ingestion resumed without dimension errors. Thanks! :tada:

Maya: I'll follow up with a short postmortem and the billing audit. For customers: best practice checklist we'll send out — pin variants, avoid mixing prefixes that map to shared cache keys, and prefer server-side `no-store` header during model migrations.

acme-sre: Appreciate the quick turnaround. Saved our nightly pipeline.

Maya: Closing the thread after the billing audit. Feel free to re-open if anything else crops up.
